summary: B1 gives every road wheel its own suspension row. KaguyaPyCore gained PhysicsSuspensionRow, a vehicle-agnostic per-station row with SI units: spring, separate compression and rebound damping, a progressive bump stop, a force cap, and closed forms for static sag, critical damping and natural frequency. The existing PhysicsSuspensionSolver was unusable here because it derives a side mass as half the vehicle and cannot express six independent wheels per side. The row force is clamped to [0, maxForceN] so a passive row never pulls and the declared cap is honoured. NativeSuspensionRowTest is the B1 fixture: a chassis carrying exactly one station's sprung mass resting on one wheel on a static floor, with a real gap between wheel and hull so hull contact can never carry the spring load. It proves the wheel settles at its static sag, the guided axle stops it at full compression and full droop, the roll axis is free while the other two are locked, travel does not induce roll, and a damped row removes more vertical energy than a near-free one. On the SBW side TrackedSuspensionCompiler resolves six rows per side, each with bind wheel centre, chassis anchor on the travel axis, unit travel and axle directions, travel window, spring and damper rates, force cap and mass share. The compiler now refuses a mechanism whose static sag cannot be reached inside compression travel, whose force cap cannot carry its share, or whose axle and travel axes are not the ones the planar solver implements. 99A audit: 6 rows per side, 19878 kg sprung per side, max static sag 0.0513 m inside 0.18 m compression, minimum force margin 12.31x, 2.2 Hz with 0.65 compression and 0.45 rebound damping ratios, rows summing to the hull mass exactly. summary: Review-driven rework of the S3.2 contact assist and the S4 coast path. Three real defects were found and fixed, and two earlier claims were retracted. (1) Friction-frame degeneracy: the chassis forward was projected onto the contact plane, then crossed with the normal. On a vertical riser the projection is zero, the fallback kept a vector parallel to the normal, and the cross product collapsed, so the solver received a friction row along the normal. TrackedContactDrive.contactFrame()/projectOntoPlane() now return null instead of fabricating a direction, and applyBeltContact() leaves the contact alone in that case. (2) The vertical-riser fallback was itself a ladder: contactAssist() invented the uphill in-plane tangent and drove the belt up a face the hull was only pressed against. A GameTest run with it enabled lifted and flipped the hull and dropped it to y=-104. It is removed; contactAssist() now returns null for a zero projection. Consequence: the previous 'one-block climb passes' result came from that ladder, not from a real belt climb. The positive S3.2 gate is NOT met and the case was rewritten as an explicit negative result. (3) Step measurement: rise was measured from the wheel bottom, which penetrates the floor, so a real one-block ledge read as taller than one block and was refused. sampleStepTerrain() now uses supportHeightUnder() (highest real support top under the wheel footprint). Additional corrections: obstacle identity is now StepFaceKey (near-face position along the approach plus top height) so a wide ledge built from many columns is assisted once per substep instead of once per column; stackedOnSameFootprint refuses a box resting on an equally sized box, closing the ratchet where the second course of a two-block wall looks like a legal one-block step; per-substep assist diagnostics reset in beginSupportWindow so a stale 'assist fired' can never be read, with a separate persistent last-write record for inspection; the duplicate publishStepPose() call in VehicleBody.preStep was removed. GameTest evidence gaps were closed: the two-block wall case no longer gives the chassis a terrain collision mask (it previously could stop because the hull hit the wall), and both the wall and pit cases now call the production game-thread sampler every tick and assert that candidates were actually observed. The pit case now has a real floor with a bounded bottom. S4 coast: two velocity-target implementations of RollingResistance were measured and both injected energy. Decaying the run's own surface speed braked the hull from 0.98 to 0.15 m/s in 20 ticks; targeting the hull speed acted as a throttle and accelerated the vehicle by 18% over 120 ticks after release. RollingResistance is therefore NOT implemented: COAST clears the conveyor target only, and TrackedContactDrive.coastTarget() is retained as an uncalled candidate. Results: tracked unit/native 180/180 pass; GameTest 51/51 required tests pass; git diff --check clean. S3.2 remains in_progress with its positive gate failed, and S4 has no rolling resistance.

Still missing: consecutive steps, per-frame suspension travel logging during assist, a real rolling-resistance implementation that is passive, and manual pause point C.
